text: Request #1 fixed: `Interval.fromISO` called `DateTime.fromISO` on the duration half of the string, so under `Settings.throwOnInvalid` a valid `start/duration` (or `duration/end`) input threw instead of returning an Interval. It now guards both endpoint parses with try/catch and falls back to the Duration path. Also fixed the malformed message "can't be parsed asISO 8601" -> "as ISO 8601". Full suite: 892 passed, only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures remain (they fail before my change too).

Request #2 fixed: in `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS` reverted the 1900-year offset with `setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which kept the day/month overflow computed by `Date.UTC` in the 19xx year (a different leap-year pattern). For years 0-99 near the century boundary (e.g. `0099-12-31` + 2 days) the result was off by a day. It now does `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`, recomputing the overflow in the real year. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({day: 2})` -> 0100-01-02 and `0100-01-02`.minus({day: 2}) -> 0099-12-31; a brute-force sweep over years 1-2400 for day/month arithmetic now matches the calendar exactly.

Request #3 fixed: `DateTime#isInDST` in `src/datetime.js` compared the current offset against `set({ month: 1 })`, i.e. the same day-of-month in January. In 1974 the US started DST on January 6, so January's offset already equalled the DST offset and every DST date in 1974 was reported as not in DST. It now compares against `set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (Jan 1, standard time). Verified: 1974 America/New_York now reports isInDST true from Jan 6 through Oct 27 and false outside that range, with no other test changes.

Request #4 fixed: the conversion matrices in `src/duration.js` were missing entries, so some unit pairs produced NaN. `casualMatrix.quarters` had no `seconds` (so `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1}).as("seconds")` gave 0 / `shiftTo("seconds")` gave NaN), and `years` had no `quarters` in either `casualMatrix` or `accurateMatrix` (so normalizing `{years, quarters}` gave NaN). Added `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to quarters and `quarters: 4` to years in both matrices. Verified: every ordered pair of units now normalizes/shifts and round-trips in both casual and longterm accuracy, and the full suite still shows only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

Request #5 fixed: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` padded the whole string including the minus sign, so a negative year was truncated into garbage: `DateTime.utc(-50, 5, 25).toISODate()` returned `0-50-05-25` instead of `-0050-05-25` (and `-5` gave `00-5-...`). It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign, keeping the "no padding needed" case intact (e.g. year 36000 still formats as `36000`, `-118040` as `-118040`). Verified across negative/zero/positive years for toISODate, toISO, toISOWeekDate and toFormat("yyyy"); full suite still 892 passed with only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.

Request #6 fixed: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` was hardcoded to `true`, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")`) claimed to be valid. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`. As a result `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("blorp") })` (and setZone/fromObject with such a zone) is invalid with reason "unsupported zone", while `FixedOffsetZone.instance(5)` / `utcInstance` stay valid. Full suite: 892 passed, only the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures.
